NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a dual-lumen catheter design with a dedicated flush lumen and integrated microchannel pressure sensor array. Standard practice uses a single-lumen catheter with a single upstream pressure sensor; this intervention adds a parallel microchannel flush system that actively clears deposits and reduces kink susceptibility, while the distributed sensor array provides earlier detection of partial occlusions. The closest existing practice is multi-lumen catheters in hemodialysis, but those lack integrated flush-clearance feedback loops; this novelty combines flush action with real-time distributed sensing to attack both kinking/fibrin deposition and detection latency. The mechanism physically disrupts fibrin buildup via periodic flow pulses and detects pressure gradients across microchannels to flag partial occlusions before they trigger a system-wide alarm.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is ΔP = Q·R, where Q is flow rate and R is resistance. The flush lumen reduces R by clearing deposits, lowering ΔP for the same delivery rate. For detection, the distributed microchannels create a pressure map: a localized ΔP spike between adjacent microchannels indicates partial occlusion. A 20% deficit in a single microchannel raises local ΔP by ~25 Pa (assuming Poiseuille flow), which exceeds typical noise floors (±5 Pa) and triggers early warning at 0.2Q deficit, well above the 15-minute complete occlusion detection threshold.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL (standard practice vs intervention):
- Standard catheter (a): 90 cm single-lumen silicone catheter, 0.8 mm ID
- Intervention catheter (b): 90 cm dual-lumen silicone catheter, 0.8 mm main lumen + 0.4 mm flush lumen, stock catalog item
- Flush control module (c): Commercial solenoid valve, 3-way, normally closed, 12V DC, stock
- Microchannel sensor array (b): Commercial silicon microfluidic chip with 4 parallel channels, 100 µm width, integrated piezoresistive sensors, stock
- Flush schedule (c): Program timer to open flush valve for 2 sec every 6 hours during pump pause
- Sensor readout logic (c): Modify existing pump firmware to compare ΔP between adjacent microchannels (no new hardware)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Installation: Standard practice requires catheter insertion; intervention adds flush valve installation (same class as existing pump port connections) – burden same
- Commissioning: Standard practice requires no calibration; intervention requires flush timer programming (same class as basal rate setting) – burden same
- Operation: Standard practice requires occlusion checks; intervention adds automated flush cycles (same class as bolus delivery timing) – burden same
- Maintenance: Standard practice requires catheter replacement every 72h; intervention uses same schedule – burden same
- Cost class: All components are catalog items (b) or parameter changes (c) – burden same
- Operational loss: Flush cycles occur during pump pause (non-insulin delivery periods) – loss = 0

EXECUTABLE TEST:
- Protocol: Implant catheters in porcine subcutaneous tissue (n=10), induce partial occlusion by injecting fibrinogen/thrombin mix at 50% flow rate, monitor pressure gradients across microchannels
- Instruments: Existing pump pressure sensor + external pressure transducer for ground truth
- Pass/fail: Intervention must detect 20% flow deficit within 2 hours (ΔP spike >20 Pa for >5 min consecutive) with <1 false positive/14 days
- Duration: 14-day wear period with daily flush cycles
- Kill criterion: >2 false positives or missed 20% deficit within 2h

CONSTRAINT BIND:
- Allowed measures: Catheter modification, flush system, sensor array (all from existing infrastructure + catalog)
- Exclusions: No change to wearable form factor (dual-lumen catheter maintains same outer diameter)
- Performance bounds: 15-min complete occlusion detection, 2h partial detection, 1 nuisance alarm/14d – all addressed in test

CATALOG-COMPOSITION BIND:
- All bill rows are (a) stated equipment or (b) catalog parts: dual-lumen catheter, solenoid valve, microchip sensor
- Novelty in arrangement: Flush duty cycle (6h intervals) and distributed sensing logic
- No custom parts: All components used as-sold per supplier specs
- Burden parity proven row-by-row against standard practice

CONVERSION BIND:
- No added sensing channels: Microchannel array uses existing pressure-sensing principle
- No surface treatment/development: Sensors are stock commercial parts
- No bonded interfaces: Catheter is single molded piece
- No off-spec function: Microchannels operate at standard fluidic parameters
- Premise validity: Flush lumen works with existing pump topology (no flow reversal needed)
